answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a harbor charging each ship a deposit before it may dock. One cheap identity is worthless, because an attacker spawning a river of fake agents must fund every single one, and misbehavior forfeits the stake. Honest agents build reputation over time, so at the zenith of trust sit long-lived, well-bonded identities, while throwaway clones stay at the bottom, unable to outvote or outbid them.
